generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: FNA's account of the family: the leaves, at the base and on the stem, are distichous, so one stands at each node.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: FNA's account of the family: the leaves are distichous, in two ranks, their blades edgewise to the stem: an iris's fan.

traits.note: Michigan State's Botany Online account of the family, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): 6 petaloid tepals in two whorls, often united in a tube; stamens 3, opposite the outer tepals; ovary inferior (superior only in Tasmania's Isophysis), 3-locular, of 3 carpels. Iris and Sisyrinchium are regular (Sisyrinchium: the NEON biorepository's genus text, as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read); gladioli and their kin are zygomorphic.

traits.leaf_division.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 386 Iridaceae: leaves mostly narrowly linear, flattened sideways and sheathing (equitant); fruit a capsule opening by valves along its cells.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Iridaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Geosiridaceae: how long the leaves last (character 37), coded often evergreen, often deciduous. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
